definitions.explanation: A suffix attached to nouns or verb stems to indicate a person who does something or has a certain characteristic.

examples.japanese: {研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}として{働|はたら}いている。
{消費者|しょうひしゃ}のニーズを{把握|はあく}する。
{被害者|ひがいしゃ}を{支援|しえん}するプログラムがある。
examples.english: There's a program to support victims.

notes:
〜{者|しゃ} is a productive suffix used to form agent nouns (people who do something).

COMMON WORDS WITH 〜{者|しゃ}:
- {研究者|けんきゅうしゃ} - researcher
- {記者|きしゃ} - reporter
- {消費者|しょうひしゃ} - consumer
- {労働者|ろうどうしゃ} - worker
- {被害者|ひがいしゃ} - victim
- {加害者|かがいしゃ} - perpetrator
- {参加者|さんかしゃ} - participant
- {経営者|けいえいしゃ} - manager, executive
- {著者|ちょしゃ} - author
- {読者|どくしゃ} - reader

〜{者|しゃ} VS 〜{家|か} VS 〜{員|いん}:
- {者|しゃ} - general person who does/is
- {家|か} - professional, expert, specialist
- {員|いん} - member, staff, official

READING NOTE:
{者} can be read as {もの} in some words (e.g., {若者|わかもの}), but the suffix is typically {しゃ}.
